gist: Data belonging to more than 41,000 US Department of Homeland Security personnel was leaked online.
Hackers obtained employee records, operational names, and surveillance tools, reportedly via Okta.
The leak targets immigration enforcement staff amid growing public criticism and increased deportations.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A group calling itself the Department of Peace accessed and leaked details of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security personnel. Distributed Denial of Secrets published the database, named Icepick. Outlets disagree on exact numbers for Immigration and Customs Enforcement, citing nearly 6,600, about 6,600, 7,000, or roughly 10,000 records. While activists claim the data came via Okta, Okta denies its systems were compromised.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The breach exposes organisational charts, undercover operations, and surveillance tools used across agencies including border and immigration enforcement. It follows controversial immigration crackdowns, fatal shootings by agents, and official efforts to conceal staff identities while seeking to unmask public critics.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Homeland Security stated it is actively addressing the potential breach to protect personnel and will update the public when further information becomes available.

fivew: The Department of Peace obtained the data, which was published by Distributed Denial of Secrets and maia crimew.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Millions of Americans are voting in the 2026 midterm elections to decide control of Congress and key governorships. The election protection hotline received 3,000 calls on election morning, while the Department of Justice dispatched 1,000 election monitors across all states.

sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eighteen-year-old Henry Nowak was fatally stabbed in Southampton on 3 December 2025. His attacker, Vickrum Digwa, falsely claimed Nowak racially abused him. gist: Labour has ended power sharing agreements with the Green Party in eleven local councils.
The split follows a Green Party conference motion defining Zionism as a form of racism.
Labour demanded local Greens disown the motion, leading to the collapse of several local coalitions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Labour Party withdrew from local coalitions and cooperation agreements with the Green Party across eleven authorities after national Greens adopted a policy stating Zionism is racism. Labour gave an ultimatum requiring local Green groups to reject the conference motion. While six Green groups complied and retained their partnerships, eleven refused, leading Labour to end those local arrangements.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The breakdown of these local partnerships threatens to disrupt council administration and delay decisions regarding local services and budgets. It has caused division between national leadership and local councillors who argue that foreign policy should not dictate local government cooperation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Affected Green and Labour councillors must now seek alternative coalition partners or attempt to govern as minority administrations. Meanwhile, other political figures like the Liberal Democrats have also distanced themselves from the Green Party over the policy.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The government plans to double the standard length of time migrants must live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement from five to 10 years. A 10-year pathway requires earning at least £12,571 for five of the seven years before settlement. Shorter qualifying periods of three or five years apply to specific groups, including high earners, certain care workers, skilled public service workers, and people with British National (Overseas) status. Conversely, migrants who claimed certain benefits or breached rules face a 20-year wait. Additional conditions include having no criminal record, speaking good English, owing no taxpayer debt, and having a record of National Insurance contributions.

gist: Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo sold out quickly after its launch.
The company is unsure when supply will meet high demand for the device.
Supply shortages and rising memory costs are expected to continue into next year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo sold out shortly after its release, leaving the company unsure when more units will be available. Chief Executive John Ternus expressed delight at the response to the $1,999 device, despite reports of screens cracking along the fold. Apple promised to replace affected units. Meanwhile, overall annual sales rose 15% to $479bn.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: High demand and ongoing microprocessor shortages, alongside rising memory costs linked to artificial intelligence data centres, have constrained supply. Consequently, Apple has increased prices across its hardware products by around 20%.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Dustin Hoffman revealed that filming the 1967 movie The Graduate was a terrible experience. He felt uncomfortable playing Ben Braddock and described director Mike Nichols as irritable and changeable. During rehearsals and filming, co-star Katharine Ross slapped Hoffman 27 times for a scene that was not used. The next day, Hoffman punctured an eardrum while filming underwater in a swimming pool. Co-star Anne Bancroft fainted during a hot scene, whilst Hoffman was made to run repeatedly until exhausted.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Graduate launched Hoffman's career and won best director at the 40th Academy Awards despite the difficult shoot. Hoffman now views Benjamin as an alter ego for Nichols, suggesting he absorbed the director's own self-loathing during filming.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hoffman's memoir, Look at Me, co-written with Ariel Levy, is set to be published on 10 November.

timeline.text: Celebrity loses injunction bid but will stay anonymous pending appeal

gist: A celebrity lost a High Court bid to permanently block reports of alleged misconduct.
An interim injunction maintaining anonymity remains active to allow a potential appeal.
The judge ruled that the man's suicide risk did not justify restraining publication.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed a celebrity's request for a permanent injunction to block ITN and the Guardian from releasing allegations of sexual misconduct and abuse of power involving young women and girls. The man denied the claims, arguing that publication would violate his human rights and cause him to take his own life.

sections.heading: Why it matters

timeline.text: UK cuts aid to Commonwealth countries despite warm words at Chogm summit

gist: The UK government is drastically cutting overseas aid to Commonwealth countries.
Funding will drop from £546m in 2024-25 to £131m in 2028-29.
The cuts affect many impoverished and highly indebted nations despite warm diplomatic words.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The UK government has slashed overseas aid to Commonwealth nations. Funding for countries with bilateral aid programmes is set to fall from £546m in 2024-25 to £131m in 2028-29. Extremely poor and indebted countries, such as Sierra Leone and Rwanda, face major reductions alongside better-off developing nations.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Critics point out a stark contrast between ministers' warm rhetoric at the Chogm summit and the reality of severe financial cutbacks. Charities warn that the reductions will harm vulnerable families, children, and biodiversity initiatives at a time of high global need.

fivew: The UK government, King Charles and Andy Burnham.
The UK government slashed overseas aid to Commonwealth countries.
At the Chogm summit in Antigua.
The aid budget is being cut back overall, targeting rapidly developing middle income nations as well as poorer countries.

quotes.text: UK aid to Commonwealth countries has fallen dramatically in recent years, with further cuts on the horizon.

quotes.text: The UK government has really dropped the ball when it comes to the aid budget

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scotland suffered a defeat at home to Slovenia, leading to deflation after an earlier promising start under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli. Pocognoli named his latest squad, welcoming back Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Kieran Tierney while handing James Penrice a first call-up. Lennon Miller was dropped again.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Scotland are third in Nations League Group B1 and need points to avoid relegation or reach promotion play-offs. Time with the players is also critical ahead of Euro 2028 qualification.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Scotland face a double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland to conclude their Nations League campaign. The qualifying draw for Euro 2028 takes place in Belfast on 6 December.

gist: Kimi Antonelli became the youngest F1 world champion in his second season.
Mercedes signed Antonelli after Lewis Hamilton announced his departure for Ferrari.
Antonelli overcame early struggles and crashes to dominate the championship.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Kimi Antonelli joined Formula 1 with Mercedes in 2025 after Lewis Hamilton signed for Ferrari. Following a challenging rookie season marked by mistakes and pressure, Antonelli secured multiple wins and poles to become the youngest world champion in the sport's history in only his second season.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Antonelli's rapid ascent highlights Mercedes' successful generational transition. Despite initial doubts and a difficult mid-season slump, his exceptional car control and mental turnaround proved that young talent can immediately contend at the highest level of motorsport.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Having secured the world championship and learned to manage high-level pressure with advice from figures like Roger Federer, Antonelli enters future seasons firmly established as a dominant force at the front of the F1 grid.

Morgan Rogers scored a brilliant solo goal to break the deadlock.
Chelsea coped with key absences by deploying a strikerless formation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Estevao Willian made his first Premier League start of the season in Chelsea's 2-0 victory against Manchester United. He had two goals disallowed and received a standing ovation. Morgan Rogers scored a solo goal in the second half, and Cole Palmer sealed the win from the penalty spot.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Chelsea faced a shortage of options with eight players missing, including first-choice striker Joao Pedro. The impressive performances of Estevao and Rogers eased pressure on head coach Xabi Alonso after recent defeats and proved the team can find creative attacking solutions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Estevao's standout display will increase pressure on Xabi Alonso to keep the winger in the starting lineup for upcoming matches.

fivew: Chelsea defeated Manchester United two-nil in the Premier League.
Estevao Willian and Morgan Rogers secured the victory despite a striker shortage.

gist: Everton striker Thierno Barry's home was burgled during a cup match.
The player expressed relief that his partner and toddler were not home.
Barry stated he will no longer risk his family by sharing personal life details online.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Everton striker Thierno Barry's home in Greater Manchester was burgled while he played in a Carabao Cup tie against Newcastle United on Thursday. Greater Manchester Police confirmed an ongoing investigation.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The 24-year-old Frenchman voiced relief that his partner and toddler were attending the match in the stands, noting the situation could have been much worse.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Barry stated he will stop putting his family at risk by posting about his personal life and lifestyle on social media.

timeline.text: Are Celtic club in regression amid run of six defeats in 10?

gist: Celtic suffered a surprise defeat to Falkirk, marking their sixth loss in ten matches.
Pundits and fans raised concerns over team regression, aging players, and squad tactics.
Despite recent poor form, manager Martin O'Neill noted Celtic remain top of the Premiership.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Celtic lost a Scottish Premiership match to Falkirk, recording their sixth defeat in ten matches across all competitions. Despite dominating possession and shots, Celtic failed to secure a win, following a draw against Dundee United.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The defeat allowed rivals to close the gap at the top of the table. Pundits and fans questioned the team's direction, citing injuries, player aging, and tactical confusion under manager Martin O'Neill.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Celtic face a crucial home match against Besiktas in the Europa League, which they need to win to keep progression hopes alive after starting the competition with three defeats.

fivew: Celtic experienced a defeat against Falkirk amid a run of poor form.
Deficiencies across the team and a toll of age and injury on key players were cited.

quotes.text: Martin's not going to say it, of course, but the club is in regression, the team is in regression
This time last year, we were in a worse position.
